title: What If We Tried to Cool Yellowstone's Supervolcano?

scenes.text: What if we cooled a supervolcano? NASA scientists studied exactly that for Yellowstone.
Yellowstone leaks about 6 gigawatts of heat. Removing around 35 percent of it could, in theory, prevent a supereruption.
The plan: drill roughly 10 kilometers down beside the magma and pump water through at high pressure.
The water would return to the surface at about 350 degrees Celsius, hot enough to run a geothermal power plant.
NASA put the cost at about 3.5 billion dollars, with electricity at roughly 10 cents a kilowatt-hour.
The catch: drilling into the magma system could, in the worst case, trigger the eruption it was meant to stop.

description:
What if we tried to cool Yellowstone's supervolcano?
A NASA study suggested drilling about 10 kilometers down and pumping water through, but warned the drilling itself could be risky.
What should we run through next?
